title: Sales Totals with awk
description: Sum the amount column of a CSV and count its data rows into a small report.
scenario: Finance dropped /var/log/app/sales.csv on the ops box and needs two numbers for the weekly call: the total revenue and the number of sales rows (the header line does not count). There is no spreadsheet software on the server — but awk was literally built for exactly this job.
symptoms: sales.csv has a header line that must not be counted or summed
The amount is the third comma-separated column
The report must be machine-readable: total=… and rows=… lines
The finance team needs the total formatted with exactly two decimals
mission: Create /home/intern/sales-total.txt containing `total=3373.51` and `rows=20`, computed from the CSV with awk.

hints.title: Choose a field separator
hints.content: `awk -F,` splits each line on commas, so $1 is the date, $2 the region and $3 the amount.

hints.title: Skip the header
hints.content: `NR>1` is true from the second record on — the header never enters the sum.

hints.title: Accumulate and print at END
hints.content: The pattern `{s+=$3}` accumulates; the `END {…}` block runs after the last line and prints the result. Use `printf "%.2f"` for two decimals.

hints.title: Row count
hints.content: NR is the number of records seen, so `END {print NR-1}` is the data-row count (header excluded).
